name: Vulcan language family
about: Proto-Vulcan and its branches: Ceremonial (Classical as frozen in ritual), Standard Vulcan, and Romulan. One family pack, because the branches share one proto-language and one file of sound laws. The pack only points at the live files in vulcan-conlang/; it never moves or changes them.

orthography.about: The one spelling standard for Standard Vulcan (ck > k, oy > oi, English-style ah/eh/oh > a/e/o ...)

reading.about: IPA-style reading of a Standard Vulcan form

speech.about: Spoken through Kokoro-FastAPI from the IPA reading, never from English-style spelling. Kokoro has no ɬ (Romulan ll, old lh) and no ejectives: ɬ is said as ʃl and an ejective as a stop plus a glottal stop. Stress is an open question; first-syllable stress is a placeholder.

vulcan.about: Standard Vulcan, from vulcan-conlang/docs/grammar.md and the phrasebook. Keys are dictionary keys.

romulan.about: Romulan inherits the Vulcan grammar; it has no evidentials, marks rank on the predicate, and pluralizes with -nsu (grammar.md section 11).

join_rules.note: a screen spelling's final length-h drops before a fused ending (sarlah + uth > sarlauth); uh is a vowel, not a length mark
a diphthong absorbs a like vowel (kau + uth > kauth, sharshei + ik > sharsheik)

vulcan.pro_drop: subject and object drop when context makes them clear
vulcan.adpositions: prepositions; direction toward is the suffix -fi
vulcan.polar_questions: auxiliary fronted, or initial particle kuth
vulcan.auxiliaries: Aux-V (kup, shul, wo, sei, dungi before the verb)
vulcan.negation: preverbal particle suhk; one negative per clause
vulcan.comparison: standard of comparison before the quality (X Y t'ei li/osh ADJ)
vulcan.object_marking: differential: -wizh on the last word of a definite or human object; may drop for an indefinite thing in casual speech

morphology.affixes: mostly suffixing; prefix ki'- marks completed

vulcan.tense_aspect: bare present, -pil ongoing, -un past, ki'- completed, dungi future
vulcan.copula: none in descriptions; wim for identity
obligatory_marking: another person's emotion needs an evidential (Standard)
vulcan.speech_levels: -mush honorific, -fum humble, cheil before a title, ihk-ve honored you, final suh formal; all drop between t'hy'la
vulcan.experiencer: Standard: the emotion is the subject and the speaker a location (Sik tok nash-ve kon); Classical: the experiencer is the subject

romulan.rank_marking: mode endings on every predicate: -'nra said up to a superior, -ha down to an inferior
romulan.evidentials: none; hwil marks 'not to be repeated', khnai 'it is whispered'

open_questions.question: Standard Vulcan is verb-final but has prepositions, noun-before-genitive, noun-before-relative and auxiliary-before-verb. Most verb-final languages have the opposite on each (Persian is the real-world model for Vulcan's mix). Why?
open_questions.proposal: Classical or Tribal Vulcan was consistently head-final; the suffixes -fi and -wizh are its fossilized postpositions. Not adopted.

open_questions.question: Should ekh split into an inclusive and an exclusive 'we'?
Stress or pitch accent, and does any branch develop tone as the apostrophe consonants weaken?
Script type for each era, and the era at which spelling froze.

expand.note: Vulcan is built by its own tools. utp.py apply appends approved compounds to derivations.csv and roots to meanings.csv, then runs these steps.
